transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. The main reason I came in is that at work I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish my claim reviews. It’s been hard to stay put and get through them.
Do you feel restless or have a hard time staying seated, even when you know you should stay at your workstation?
Yes. That’s actually the main reason I came in. I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I need to stay there and finish my claim reviews. It’s been getting in the way.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks, like your claim reviews, even when you’re sitting at your desk? Or do you get distracted easily by things around you?

Yeah, I do. Even if I’m sitting there, if people near me start talking about another claim, or I suddenly remember some random errand I need to do, my attention just kind of slides off what I’m reading. Then I realize I didn’t take in the section at all and I have to reread it a few times.
When you think back to when you were a child, did you also have trouble staying focused or sitting still for long periods, or was this something that started more recently as an adult?

It wasn’t totally new as an adult. Looking back, in elementary school my teachers would write things like that I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets, miss instructions, and need reminders to finish my classwork. So I guess the focus part has been there for a long time.
Do you also notice these difficulties with staying focused and sitting still in other parts of your life, like at home, in meetings, or during conversations?

Yeah, in longer meetings or trainings especially. I’ll be trying to pay attention, but I’m usually bouncing my leg, clicking a pen, or shifting around in the chair. I try to make it look like I’m focused, but I’m definitely fidgeting a lot.
Outside of work and meetings, do you also have trouble focusing or sitting still at home, like when you're watching TV, reading, or trying to relax?

Yeah, it happens at home too. Like if I’m reading something and someone nearby starts talking, or I suddenly remember some random thing I need to do, I just lose the thread. Then I realize I didn’t actually take in what I read, so I have to go back over the same section a few times.
Have you ever noticed these symptoms of inattention and restlessness significantly affecting other areas of your life, like relationships, household responsibilities, or personal goals?

Yeah, mostly with work goals. My supervisor put me on performance coaching because my claim files are falling behind, and they’ve started questioning my accuracy. That’s been pretty stressful, because I was trying to get onto the senior adjuster track, and now I’m worried I might lose that chance.
Over the past few weeks or months, have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so, not really. I’ve been stressed and frustrated about things, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling hopeless or losing interest in stuff I normally like.
Have you ever found yourself bothered by unwanted, intrusive thoughts that keep coming back, or do you feel the need to do certain things repeatedly to ease your anxiety?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I get stressed about things, but I don’t really have thoughts that keep coming back like that, and I don’t feel like I have to repeat certain actions to calm myself down.
Outside of difficulty focusing, do you often feel an inner sense of agitation or a need to be constantly moving, like you can’t relax even when you want to?

Yeah, I do notice that sometimes. In longer trainings or team meetings, I’m usually bouncing my leg, clicking my pen, or shifting around in the chair. I’ll be trying to look like I’m paying attention and staying still, but I just keep moving without really thinking about it.
Can you think of times in your life, outside of work and meetings, when you’ve had trouble focusing or felt restless, such as when you were in school, or in social situations?

Yeah, looking back, it wasn’t really new. In elementary school, teachers would write things like I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets, miss instructions, or need reminders to actually finish my classwork. At the time I think it was just treated like I wasn’t trying hard enough, but it was definitely there.
Do you often find yourself talking more than usual, interrupting others during conversations, or acting without thinking things through?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’m usually the type to talk over people on purpose, but I can lose track of when it’s my turn sometimes. Acting without thinking… maybe once in a while, but nothing that really stands out to me as a big pattern.
Have you ever found yourself doing things very quickly without thinking them through, like making sudden decisions or acting on impulse, even if it wasn’t something you normally would do?

I don’t think that’s a major thing for me. I mean, I can make a quick choice here and there, like anyone, but I can’t really think of a pattern where I’m suddenly doing things that are out of character or causing problems because I didn’t think first.
Have your difficulties with focus and restlessness ever caused problems in your social life, at home, or in other important areas outside of work?

Yeah, it has. The biggest problem has been at work, honestly. My supervisor put me on performance coaching because my claim files are falling behind, and they’ve started questioning my accuracy. That’s been stressful because I was trying to get onto the senior adjuster track, and now I’m worried I could lose that chance.
